left: The P0 kitchen has no stove, table, pot or lantern: the five writes were removed, not moved, because every cell in the room is interior air that shell-west.mjs (line 16, g.fill(..., "air")) set and runParts locked. Lifting that lock or moving the interior air-fill to a later step belongs to the shell owner, not this part.

The same lock will block the furniture in every room part. Only P0 kitchen attempted writes; the other room parts report 0 placed and 0 refused, so they are empty for the same reason or are stubs. Their writes need checking once the lock is decided.

Off-palette: none in this part. The five blocks (smoker, furnace, crafting_table, potted_poppy, lantern) are all in palette.json, so no swap was needed.

waste.what: Working out why the five writes were refused: reading the runParts source to learn that the lock covers air, and that the shell's g.fill(..., "air") is what owns the interior cells.

waste.what: Writing out the intended layout as a comment because the fit-out cannot be placed.

waste.tool: A dry-run mode on layers() that lists the cells it would write and the lock owner, so the design can be kept and checked without placing.

Lifting that lock or moving the interior air-fill to a later step belongs to the shell owner, not this part.

The same lock will block the furniture in every room part. Only P0 kitchen attempted writes; the other room parts report 0 placed and 0 refused, so they are empty for the same reason or are stubs. Their writes need checking once the lock is decided.
The lantern at (11,4,20) hangs from y5, the upper floor layer, which the shell must leave solid for it to be placed.
Off-palette: none in this part. The five blocks (smoker, furnace, crafting_table, potted_poppy, lantern) are all in palette.json, so no swap was needed.

waste.what: Working out why the five writes were refused: reading the runParts source to learn that the lock covers air, and that the shell's g.fill(..., "air") is what owns the interior cells.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and a read of build.mjs lines 205-250 plus shell-west.mjs
waste.tool: Make parts-report.json's refusedAt entries name the owning part (e.g. 'owned by shell west, air fill') and print a one-line hint when the owner's write was air, so the cause shows without reading the library.

waste.what: Checking that each refused block is in palette.json by hand, since the palette check never runs on refused writes.
waste.tool: A `$MCD blocks --check` pass over the part's intended blocks (or palette checking of refused writes too) would have flagged off-palette ids even when the cell is locked.

waste.what: Writing out the intended layout as a comment because the fit-out cannot be placed.
waste.cost: the cell list was copied from the layers() grid by hand
waste.tool: A dry-run mode on layers() that lists the cells it would write and the lock owner, so the design can be kept and checked without placing.
